issue.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

### Problem

Source merges cannot establish which validator and host versions are released, adopted or installed, or prove that explicit legacy cutoffs and body-backed factory pickup work on the live system.

### Desired outcome

Activate body-contract triage across released validators, explicit adopter cutoffs and the factory host, and record actual compatible pickup. This issue closes only on recorded live acceptance; source merges alone cannot close it.

### Proposed approach

The independently reviewed Agent Brief comment is the implementation contract. Follow its compatibility matrix, delivery responsibilities, per-adopter inventory and cutoff, recovery and live-evidence criteria.

### Additional context

Blocked by both source issues: [Repo Canon BR #919](https://github.com/lutzseverino/repo-canon/issues/919) and [Scriptorium BR-SC #148](https://github.com/lutzseverino/scriptorium/issues/148). Their normal releases, compatible adoption and authorized host access remain required acceptance inputs. Source pull requests link this live ticket without a closing reference.

The owner's 2026-11-08T19:07Z “yes” approved plans 19 and 20 as amended by grill G3, including independent review, filing and revision-bound readiness. The contract copies its relied-on dated decisions; no new owner intent is inferred.

Use the serial direct-worker lane with `factory:skip`, `priority:normal` and `model:gpt-6.1-sol@high`. Repo Canon is not factory-served. Scheduling relations are not blockers. Readiness permits neither premature activation nor pickup before the contract's prerequisites hold.

comments.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Activate body-contract triage across released validators, explicit adopter cutoffs and the factory host, and record actual compatible pickup; source merges alone cannot close this ticket.

**Current behavior:**
Inspected source heads are Canon `bd4b59a6fde6ee252a3904775f8854cdd4e9960f`
and Scriptorium `1ec2c8ba5c5794a5cb2fdd9a530cb2d363ab6c18` (3.0.1). They
still use comment-only factory triage contracts/provenance. No inspection of
those sources proves which package is installed on a host or adopted by a
repository. Two separate source changes must supply a prepared/body-mode
validator with durable cutoff eligibility and a bridge host with both body
publication and body-backed `triageBacked`/readiness consumption.

**Desired behavior:**
Deliver the rollout through the two source contracts, in repo-canon
“Implement issue-body triage contracts with durable legacy eligibility” and
in scriptorium “Publish and consume body-backed factory triage contracts.”
Both are native blockers of this repo-canon live-acceptance ticket when
filed. Record their actual repository issue/PR URLs; add further native
release/adoption/host-delivery blockers if separately ticketed. No issue
number is implied here. Source PRs close only their source issues and link
this ticket without closing references. This ticket cannot close on any merge.

Inventory every repository served by the target factory host, including
Canon and Scriptorium's own delivery repositories and held/skip-routed ones;
record each installed Canon release/full SHA, factory config version/run
kinds, result format/mode, host reader/poster capability and authorized
delivery route. Record other selected adopters and non-factory consumers
before switching them. The initial acceptance scope is every repository
served by that host plus every adopter explicitly enrolled in this rollout;
non-enrolled adopters stay in prepared legacy mode and are listed as such.
Never claim an unknown adopter or host upgraded from a source merge. Record
actual signed/released artifact identities or the repository's normal release
identity, installed host version/SHA and adopter destination-base versions.
Choose concrete release numbers from the merged sources and record them
before installation. The body cutoff is per adopter, not a global release
timestamp and not the first validator run after upgrade.

The compatibility contract is:

| Host capability | Adopter validator state | Allowed publication/pickup and recovery |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Old: v1 reader, comment poster (including inspected 3.0.1) | Old v1 legacy validator | Existing legacy publication and pickup; source prerequisites can use the current authorized lane. |
| Old | New release, preparation mode/v1 | Existing legacy route only. Do not enable body mode or v2; install the bridge host first. |
| Old | New active body mode/v2 | Unsupported: new pickup is held by the unsupported result format; old posting is stopped by the rollout freeze/host hold. Install bridge and revalidate; never resume an old poster into this state. |
| New bridge: v1+v2 reader, dual poster | Old v1 validator | Emit legacy comments and use existing authorization. No premature body publication. |
| New bridge | Prepared validator/v1, no cutoff yet | Keep legacy route; release/adoption work remains deliverable. Drain/freeze triage before inventory and cutoff. |
| New bridge | Active validator/v2, trusted cutoff | New/revised contracts publish bodies; unchanged inventoried legacy revisions retain their contract, review and pickup route. No new/edited comment creates a contract. |
| Any | Unknown/malformed format, unreadable facts, missing/incomplete cutoff or mismatched capabilities | Hold affected publication/pickup, identify the missing proof, restore compatible components/receipt and re-evaluate. No guessed acceptance or implicit grandfathering. |

V2 means `repo-canon/issue-contract-state/v2`, with status/revision/source,
current ready-event approval, cutoff selection state and verified
revision/run/attestation association. V1 keeps its old meaning. The bridge's
body reader requires the approved current ready event and matching
configured-author attestation; the generic body-source freshness check alone
is insufficient. It passes that verified factory status through
`Issue.ready.triage`, role/refusal checks and factory implement admission.
Ordinary authorized-person readiness remains available; it does not bypass
an unsupported host result format or an unready/blocked contract.

Follow this order, recording evidence and the delivery actor for each step:

1. Publish the two merged source contracts, wire schema/fixtures, passing
   source checks and normal releases. Keep Canon's new release in preparation
   mode/v1. Existing compatible factory lanes can deliver these prerequisites;
   source closure does not depend on deployment. Check destination-base
   tooling and all self-hosted delivery repositories, not just PR heads.
2. Install the bridge Scriptorium host while adopters are still v1 legacy.
   A host operator with the established host access performs installation;
   no sandbox agent gains host/issue-write credentials. Prove new-host/old-
   validator legacy publication and pickup before proceeding. If the factory
   cannot deliver its own prerequisite, use the already-authorized manual
   gap path under installed rules or hold for an authorized operator; record
   exactly who can complete it rather than assuming the broken factory can.
3. Adopt the released prepared Canon validator, guidance/skills and required
   workflow/configuration inputs per repository, retaining v1/legacy mode.
   Prove installed source identity and mode, including Canon and Scriptorium
   themselves. Old-host/prepared-validator remains compatible if encountered;
   it is not permission to activate before the bridge is installed.
4. Freeze new/revised triage publication from every poster, manual and
   factory. Stop new triage admission and drain completed/in-flight results
   under the legacy route, or hold them explicitly for fresh body-mode
   triage; include preserved results that may retry after restart. Existing
   unchanged accepted implement/review work can continue where the installed
   admission/hold policy allows it. If only a repository-wide hold exists,
   record that broader pause and the operator who can remove it. During this
   boundary the operator delivers cutoff/adoption steps, not a triage worker.
5. Capture and verify a complete trusted cutoff receipt: repository identity,
   release/SHA, epoch, every selected eligible open legacy comment identity,
   exact content/edit revision and existing notice/acceptance association.
   Include unapproved/held issues without granting acceptance. Re-read for
   concurrent changes; an incomplete/raced inventory cannot activate.
   Persist eligibility and migrated/retired state outside replaceable contract
   text, so upgrades, feedback deletion and body deletion cannot reset it.
6. With the freeze still in force, activate that adopter's body mode and v2
   results, re-evaluate the inventoried contracts and verify unchanged
   approvals/current ready events survive. Inspect the mode/cutoff/legacy
   diagnostic. After both host capabilities and installed validator agree,
   reopen triage publication/admission in body mode. A waiting old result
   cannot fall back to posting a new comment contract. Repeat per enrolled
   adopter; repositories not yet switched keep their legacy lane.
7. Demonstrate live read-only triage to body publication, exact-revision
   notice, matching host attestation, applicable fresh acceptance, current
   approved result and actual implement pickup. Record the implement run's
   identity and selected source/revision; do not stop at a ready label,
   notice, boolean or approved result. Retain independent review and all
   admission/blocker/role rules. Record that a same/unknown intake-writer
   run and absent/tampered/mismatched body proof do not grant factory pickup;
   use controlled test issues for live negative cases, not arbitrary edits
   to accepted production work.

There is no interval in the supported sequence where an old poster emits
new comment contracts that an active validator rejects: retain the old route
until the freeze; resume only with a proven body poster/reader. An accidental
old-host/active-validator mismatch is visibly held and repaired forward to
the bridge before any poster resumes. Before cutoff, rollback to legacy
components/mode is allowed while the trusted inventory remains uncommitted.
After cutoff, retain the cutoff/migration records and compatible validator;
restore the bridge or repair it forward. Do not roll back to a validator that
can bless new comment contracts or resurrect retired ones. If host recovery
is unavailable, keep the affected repository held, name the authorized
operator/manual route and its prerequisites, and leave this ticket open.
No fabricated proof or forced migration is a recovery path.

Retain support and stored eligibility for unchanged grandfathered revisions
without an expiry date. A legacy contract migrates on its next revision,
preserving one verbatim original request, publishing a new body notice and
requiring fresh applicable acceptance. A newer comment cannot override it;
deleting the body cannot restore it. Live evidence must show legacy
retention, first migration and a later body edit, alongside restart/upgrade
retention of the cutoff and retired state. Any future removal of the legacy
route needs its own accepted change; it is not hidden in this activation.

**Key interfaces:**

- Released Canon validator/guidance, installed adopter mode/cutoff and durable
  source-selection history; actual native source/release/activation blockers.
- Released/installed Scriptorium host, result poster and v1/v2 provenance
  reader, original intake writer, current ready-event approval and actual
  readiness/admission/pickup outcome.
- Repository-facing activation evidence: release/adoption/host identities,
  compatibility table, delivery actor, freezes/holds, issue/event/run links,
  exact revisions, retained legacy receipts and recovery results. Secrets
  and host-only logs are not the sole acceptance input.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] Both source tickets and any required delivery tickets have actual
  repository-facing URLs/native blockers; source PRs do not close this issue.
  Public wire schema/fixtures, releases and passing source checks are linked.
- [ ] The host-served/enrolled adopter inventory is complete, with installed
  versions/SHAs, modes, result/config versions, enabled run kinds and who can
  deliver each intervening state. Self-hosted Canon/Scriptorium and
  destination-base tooling retain a usable delivery or explicit held route.
- [ ] Record new-host/old-validator and old-host/prepared-validator legacy
  compatibility, and old-host/active-validator refusal/recovery. Unsafe
  combinations are exercised with source fixtures or a controlled deployment;
  no production outage is required. Unknown proof fails closed.
- [ ] Record drain/freeze, cutoff inventory and race verification, per-adopter
  switch and revalidation, and the point publication resumes. Installed mode,
  cutoff and selected eligibility are observable. No new legacy posting can
  escape through retry/restart during or after the switch.
- [ ] A controlled live journey on an enrolled factory repository shows the
  actual read-only triage result becoming a body contract with one original,
  matching attestation/notice, fresh applicable acceptance and current
  approved result, followed by actual implement pickup. Record issue/run/
  event links and exact source/revision. End-to-end source integration tests
  alone cannot replace this live evidence.
- [ ] Live controlled negative evidence and focused source fixtures together
  show absent/stale/tampered/mismatched proof and same/unknown intake writer
  cannot authorize factory pickup; ordinary authorized-person acceptance and
  triage-off behavior retain their rules. No app-authorship shortcut is used.
- [ ] Demonstrate an unchanged eligible legacy contract/approval continuing,
  its next revision migrating to the body with a fresh notice/acceptance,
  a later edit invalidating readiness, and deletion not resurrecting legacy.
  Record retained cutoff/migration state through host restart and validator
  upgrade/re-evaluation; source fixtures cover destructive feedback/body
  deletion and edit-and-restore cases without damaging real accepted work.
- [ ] Every enrolled repository is active/compatible; any non-enrolled
  adopter is explicitly listed in preparation mode. An unresolved held
  enrolled repository or missing live proof leaves this issue open. Record
  the tested recovery path and final host/adopter versions on this issue.

**Out of scope:**
Changing the approved contract home/legacy promise; source implementation
hidden inside activation; mass migration; new credential/role/merge policy;
claiming every adopter in existence upgraded; closing #840/#841/#866 by
association. Application source tests/Docker builds need not be rerun here
when linked exact-source evidence already passes; run only the controlled
compatibility/journey checks needed to establish deployed behavior.

Triage notes:

- **Path:** live acceptance of two source contracts; host access requirements
  follow the installed human/manual routing rules. No source merge is proof
  of activation and no readiness is granted by this draft.
- **Available inputs:** this entire contract; repository-facing Canon and
  Scriptorium source/companion briefs, their PRs/releases/schema/fixtures,
  Canon ADRs 0029/0030/0035 and Scriptorium ADRs 0007/0008;
  [Canon #841](https://github.com/lutzseverino/repo-canon/issues/841),
  [#840](https://github.com/lutzseverino/repo-canon/issues/840) and
  [#866](https://github.com/lutzseverino/repo-canon/issues/866).
  Publish non-secret installed-state evidence and delivery assignments on
  this issue before starting dependent switches; no host-only record is a
  required implementation input.
- **Verification:** fetched/read Canon `bd4b59a6fde6ee252a3904775f8854cdd4e9960f`
  and Scriptorium `1ec2c8ba5c5794a5cb2fdd9a530cb2d363ab6c18` via
  `git show origin/main`. Current host code has run kinds, read-only triage,
  result posting and v2 config compatibility, but the readiness provenance
  reader is comment-only. No live host/adopter state or actual pickup was
  inspected or claimed. No prior-rejection tree or existing BR activation
  issue was identified; #841 is a general planning finding, not this rollout.
- **Owner decision, 2026-11-06, G2 D1, approved about 21:42Z, “Agreed to all”:**
  “One home for the implementation contract: the issue body”; “Triage writes
  the Agent Brief over the body and keeps the reporter's text verbatim under
  ‘Original request’.” Approved migration promise: “Open issues whose
  contract is a brief comment keep it until their next revision, which moves
  it into the body.” Public decision: ADR 0035/#874. Cutoff retention gives
  that promise an operational boundary; it does not expire unchanged issues.
- **Existing authorization decision, 2026-11-03, Canon ADR 0030:** “as long
  as it did not write the issue”; “when triage is off, readiness still comes
  from a person.” Scriptorium ADR 0008 records “the host, not the agent,
  posts” and “triage is read-only and only review may merge.” Actual pickup
  must preserve both boundaries.
- **Existing closure rule, verified 2026-11-09, CONTRIBUTING:** “a source
  ticket, which closes when its pull request merges” and “a live-acceptance
  ticket, blocked by the source ticket, which closes only on its recorded
  live acceptance.” This ticket is that independently closing live contract.
- **Inferred implementation boundary, 2026-11-09:** “Bridge host first,
  prepared adoption next, then frozen inventory and explicit per-adopter
  cutoff, then verified body publication and pickup.” This preserves the
  approved legacy exception and avoids changing either side before its
  consumer can read it. Concrete versions, inventory and delivery actors are
  required activation facts, not new owner intent or guessed release pins.
- **Dependencies:** blocked by both source tickets and availability of their
  normal releases, compatible adoption and authorized host access. Record
  actual native blocker links at filing and expand them for separately
  ticketed delivery steps. Source closures remain independent of live proof.
- **Model:** `model:gpt-6.1-sol@high` for compatibility/evidence review; live
  work follows installed host-access routing and operator authority.
- **Owner questions:** none established. If an enrolled target, access grant
  or delivery route requires a new owner choice, mark `gap: owner`, ask the
  specific question and recommend keeping that repository held until its
  authorized route is recorded. Never infer a new grant from this contract.
